title: rearchitect-prefill-decode-handoff-with-token-bucket-pipelining
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce a token-bucket based pipelined handoff between prefill and decode stages to reduce tail latency and improve throughput. Backwards-compatible config flags allow staged rollout and tuning for Dedicated clusters. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Context: We observed persistent tail latency spikes when prefill-heavy workloads interacted with decode burst traffic (especially for long-context and interactive chat flows). Existing handoff relies on ad-hoc queue draining which either starves decodes or causes prefill bursts to monopolize GPU kernels.
Motivation: Create a predictable, throughput-friendly handoff that preserves low median latency while reducing 95/99th percentile tail without changing model kernels.
Design summary:
- Introduces per-executor token-buckets that govern prefill admission into the decode-facing pipeline. Buckets accumulate credits based on dynamic rate estimates and available KV cache warmness.
- Implements a lightweight handshaking protocol between PrefillStage and DecodeStage: Prefill offers chunk tokens; Decode accepts when capacity exists; declined tokens are returned and trigger a short backoff.
- Adds a small in-memory ring buffer (handshake window) to smooth sudden bursts and allow continuous batching inside decode kernels.
- Scheduler updates: a new scheduling priority class prefill_handoff that the dispatcher uses to prefer short-prefill-chunks for low-latency paths while allowing larger chunked prefill on lower priority.
- KV cache policy: soft-evict thresholds extended to prefer retaining recently-handshaken prefixes; prefetch hints propagate through the handshake to warm KV entries for imminent decodes.
Backwards compatibility: All features are guarded behind runtime feature flags (runtime.prefill_token_bucket and runtime.prefill_handshake_window). Defaults are off for Private installs and enabled behind a gradual rollout on Hosted and Dedicated.
Performance: Benchmarked on benchlab with mixed chat trace (70% short queries, 30% long-context). Results:
- median latency for interactive decode path improved by ~18%
- p95 improved by ~27%
- overall tokens/sec increased by ~7% on p3-xlarge-equivalent clusters
- KV cache hit rate improved by ~5 percentage points for warmed conversational sessions
Implementation highlights:
- runtime/scheduler/token_bucket.h/cpp: token bucket implementation with cumulative fairness and dynamic refill based on measured decode drain rate.
- runtime/pipeline/handshake_manager.{cc,h}: handshake orchestration and ring buffer management.
- runtime/pipeline/prefill_executor.cpp: splits prefill into adjustable chunk sizes, attaches token IDs for traceability.
- runtime/pipeline/decode_executor.cpp: non-blocking accept/reject path for handshake tokens; integrates with continuous-batching loop.
- runtime/kvcache/soft_evict_policy.cpp: prioritizes entries tied to recent handshake tokens.
- tests/benchmark/bench_prefill_decode_integration.py: new workload harness and end-to-end perf assertions.
Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for token bucket corner cases (zero refill, burst pressure)
- Integration tests to assert no deadlocks during handshake failures
- Benchmarks with and without kernel coalescing to isolate scheduler effects
- Canary rollout to 5% Hosted and 2 Dedicated clusters with telemetry gating (latency + errors)
Observability and operations:
- New metrics: prefill.token_offer_rate, prefill.token_accept_rate, prefill.handshake_rejects, prefill.window_occupancy
- Tracing spans for handshake offer/accept paths (trace keys pref/handshake)
- Console flag controls for bucket refill weight and handshake window size
Rollout plan:
- Experimental in main behind flags
- Canary on low-traffic clusters for 48 hours, monitor p99/p95/p50, errors, backlog sizes
- Gradual ramp controlled by canary automation and manual checks
Potential risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mis-tuned buckets starve decodes. Mitigation: conservative defaults, auto-dial backoff on reject storms.
- Risk: additional locking in handshake manager introduces contention. Mitigation: lock-free ring buffer and optimistic accepts; measured contention <2% in benchlab.
Checklist:
- [x] Token bucket impl
- [x] Handshake protocol
- [x] Scheduler integration
- [x] KV soft-evict hints
- [x] Tests and bench harness
- [x] Telemetry and Console knobs
- [x] Docs snippet for ops

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you add a short-circuit when bucket capacity is zero to avoid offering tokens and reduce cross-thread wakeups?
Author (Maya Chen): Added fast-path in token_bucket.cpp so offers are no-ops when capacity==0; included microbenchmark showing wakeup reduction.
Sofia Morales: The backoff multiplier looked aggressive during load tests; can we make it adaptive based on recent accept ratio?
Author (Maya Chen): Switched to an adaptive multiplier that decays toward 1.0 if accept ratio > 0.7; updated unit tests and bench results.
Liam O'Neal: Please ensure metrics include 'handshake_rejects' with tag reasons (capacity|kv_cold|policy).
Author (Maya Chen): Added tagged rejects and a small breaking-out in console to surface top reject reasons for ops.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in default settings. Operators should tune runtime.prefill_token_bucket.refill_rate and runtime.prefill_handshake_window.size for high-concurrency Dedicated pools. Follow the ops doc for rollback steps if metrics regress.
